diverge.why: The JVM exposes bytes allocated per thread through com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean, but no count of allocations. JFR samples allocation events rather than counting them, so a per-iteration total is an estimate that changes with the sampling rate.
diverge.remedy: A counter alongside getThreadAllocatedBytes. bench-max-bytes is implemented, and holds a ceiling on the same behaviour by weight rather than by count.

diverge.why: The JVM reports bytes allocated per thread and no count of allocations, for the reason the bench-max-allocs entry gives, so there is no count per call to hold to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: The counter beside getThreadAllocatedBytes that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.remedy: The counter beside getThreadAllocatedBytes that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.remedy: The counter beside getThreadAllocatedBytes that bench-max-allocs needs.

limits.what: Reads the heap used of the MemoryMXBean after System.gc, under the Serial, the Parallel and the G1 collector. Under -XX:+DisableExplicitGC, under -XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent and under any other collector the call ends with a fault. A test that runs beside the call and keeps memory reachable adds that memory to each reading.
limits.why: System.gc runs a full collection that has ended when it returns only under those three collectors without the two flags. With explicit collections off, each reading of a streaming filter contained the garbage of the call, and ZGC reports its heap in pages of 2 MiB.

limits.what: Sees coroutines launched in the scope, and the platform threads the Java artifact sees. A leaked virtual thread is not reported.
limits.why: A coroutine is tracked through its Job, which is why the Kotlin artifact supplies this rather than inheriting it. Virtual threads appear in no standard enumeration on any JVM version.

limits.what: Records every invocation and completion through one counter that all clients share, whose increment is sequentially consistent. A subject whose correctness depends on a memory barrier it lacks can pass under the recorder and fail without it.
limits.why: JVM threads, and coroutines on a dispatcher of more than one thread, run on more than one core at once. Each increment of the counter orders the recording client's memory operations against every other client's, and that order can supply the barrier that the subject lacks.

limits.what: A zone resolves through the time-zone data of the JDK that runs the test, so a ZonedDateTime can show another wall time than the definition's tzdata 2026e states. A Char reads as a char shape whose alphabet stops at the end of the Basic Multilingual Plane.
limits.why: The JDK ships its own copy of the IANA time-zone data, and an update of the JDK can contain another release. A Kotlin Char is one UTF-16 unit, so it cannot represent a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.

limits.what: A zone resolves through the time-zone data of the JDK that runs the test, as the prop.of entry states.
limits.why: The JDK ships its own copy of the IANA time-zone data, and an update of the JDK can contain another release.

surface.why: The harness owns the loop here, so setup goes in a second closure, handed to measuring, that the harness runs outside the measurement. Marking the setup in place would need the body to reach the contract it was handed to.
Kotlin cancels a coroutine through its Job, and honoursCancellation hands a subject no handle. A case has no handle to return that the code under test would read.
Kotlin cancels a coroutine through its Job, and honoursCancellation hands a subject no handle. A seat has no handle to return that the code under test would read.
The helper reads the seat's cancellation handle, and a Kotlin seat states none, for the reason the seat.cancellation entry gives.

A task of the scheduler is a coroutine on its test dispatcher, and kotlinx.coroutines.yield() suspends the coroutine at a point the dispatcher sees, so the scheduler needs no member of its own for it.

records.artifact: The JUnit Platform's report entries, which a Gradle test task of Gradle 9.4 or later writes to build/test-results/<task>/TEST-<class>.xml, one file per test class. kotlin.test runs on JUnit Jupiter under useJUnitPlatform(), and the Open Test Reporting XML of the JUnit Platform contains the same entries.
records.location: One report entry per record, in the order the records are made, written as a property element under the properties element of the test's testcase element. Its name is the kind of the record followed by the record's number in its test, such as dokimi.assert.3 or dokimi.suite.1, and its value is the record's JSON. The testcase element names the test by its classname, the test class, and its name, the test's display name.
records.status: The child of each testcase element: failure for a failed test, skipped for a skipped or aborted one, and none for a pass.
